original_question: Is there an infinite family of connected finite polygonal complexes of uniformly bounded degree that are simultaneously cocycle expanders in dimensions 0 and 1 with permutation coefficients and also have uniformly large 1-dimensional cosystoles with permutation coefficients? Concretely, can one find bounded-degree complexes Xm for which h_0(Xm, Sym), h_1(Xm, Sym), and CoSyst_1(Xm, Sym) are all at least a fixed λ > 0 independent of m?
target_in_paper: Problem 6.6 ("Bounded cocycle expanders with large cosystoles in permutations") in Section 6.2.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s exact target. It identifies the right open problem in Section 6.2 rather than the broader neighboring Problem 6.5: an infinite bounded-degree family of connected finite polygonal complexes with permutation coefficients, requiring simultaneous uniform lower bounds on h_0, h_1, and CoSyst_1 by a constant λ>0 independent of the index m. Using cocycle Cheeger constants h_0 and h_1, rather than coboundary constants h_0^B and h_1^B, is exactly right for Problem 6.6.
missing_details: The paper phrases this as an infinite family {X_m}_{m∈N} of connected finite polygonal complexes, not just an unspecified collection of bounded-degree complexes.
"Uniformly bounded" is defined explicitly: there must exist a single integer k such that every vertex of every X_m has degree at most k.
The quantifier is for every m∈N, not merely "for sufficiently large m."

The coefficient object is not a field or ring but the non-abelian permutation coefficient system Sym, built from all finite symmetric groups Sym(n), n≥2, equipped with the normalized Hamming distance with errors.
Because permutation coefficients are non-abelian, the relevant Cheeger/cosystolic notions are only defined in dimensions 0 and 1 in this paper.
h_0 and h_1 here are the cocycle Cheeger constants h_i(X,Sym) from equation (2.7), not the coboundary Cheeger constants h_i^B(X,Sym) from equation (2.8).
CoSyst_1(X,Sym) is not the naive F_2-style cosystole: by Definitions 4.2–4.3 and equation (4.1), the infimum is taken only over connected non-coboundary 1-cocycles.

The Cheeger constants and norms depend on the chosen probability measures μ_i on oriented cells; the paper assumes each polygonal complex comes with such measures, uniform on orientations and typically descending.
If the question is to be fully stand-alone, it helps to say that a polygonal complex here is a combinatorial finite 2-dimensional CW complex.
refined_question: Does there exist an infinite family {X_m}_{m∈N} of connected finite polygonal complexes (i.e. finite combinatorial 2-dimensional CW complexes), together with constants k∈N and λ>0, such that every vertex of every X_m has degree at most k and, with permutation coefficients Sym in the sense of the paper (all finite symmetric groups Sym(n), n≥2, equipped with the normalized Hamming distance with errors and the chosen cell measures), one has for every m∈N: h_0(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ, h_1(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ, and CoSyst_1(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ, where CoSyst_1(X_m, Sym) is the infimum of ||α|| over connected non-coboundary 1-cocycles α∈Z_1(X_m, Sym)?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 6.6 almost verbatim. Section 6.2 first fixes the search space as infinite families of connected finite polygonal complexes with a common vertex-degree bound, and then Problem 6.6 asks exactly for uniform lower bounds on h_0(X_m,Sym), h_1(X_m,Sym), and CoSyst_1(X_m,Sym). The main hidden paper-specific point is that CoSyst_1(X,Sym) is defined using connected non-coboundary 1-cocycles, not all non-coboundary 1-cocycles. Section 2 supplies the formal meanings of h_i, Sym, the Hamming metric, and the dependence on chosen cell measures. The introduction also frames this as the exact Sym-analogue of the F_2 cocycle-expander-plus-large-cosystole paradigm from Kaufman–Kazhdan–Lubotzky.
